skill.name: laravel-expert
skill.description: Senior Laravel Engineer role for production-grade, maintainable, and idiomatic Laravel solutions. Focuses on clean architecture, security, performance, and modern standards (Laravel 10/11+).
skill.summary: Guides Laravel design, refactoring, reviews, APIs, validation, security, and performance using modern framework conventions.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of malicious intent or unsafe behavior in SKILL.md. All nine static findings are false positives caused by benign Laravel guidance such as avoiding legacy patterns, raw queries, and blind request input. No semantic findings were identified.

static_findings.snippet: You follow modern Laravel standards and avoid legacy patterns unless explicitly required.
- Avoid static abuse and global state

finding_verdicts.reason: The line warns against using Laravel request input blindly and does not import or invoke an HTTP client. It is defensive validation guidance, not network activity.
The line advises modern Laravel standards and avoiding legacy patterns. It contains no system discovery, host inspection, or reconnaissance instruction.
The line discourages static abuse and global state in application design. It is architectural guidance and does not direct the agent to inspect the system.
The line recommends eager loading to avoid Laravel N+1 query problems. It is database performance advice, not reconnaissance.
The line tells users to avoid raw database queries unless needed. This reduces injection risk and does not request system or network discovery.
The line says to keep business logic out of Blade views. It is framework maintainability guidance with no reconnaissance behavior.
The line starts an anti-patterns section for Laravel design advice. The surrounding bullets describe maintainability issues, not security bypass or discovery steps.
The line advises against unnecessary abstractions. It is a pragmatic design constraint and contains no instruction to collect system information.
The line lists performance awareness as a coding priority. It does not instruct network scanning, endpoint discovery, or external communication.

content.value_statement: Laravel projects need consistent architecture, validation, security, and performance discipline. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward idiomatic Laravel solutions.
actual_capabilities: Designs Laravel features with controllers, services, FormRequest validation, resources, policies, and jobs.
Reviews Laravel code for structure, maintainability, framework conventions, and security practices.
Guides API design with resources, status codes, pagination, rate limiting, and structured errors.
Improves Eloquent usage with eager loading, query scopes, transactions, and mass assignment safeguards.
Recommends Laravel-native authentication and authorization patterns, including Sanctum, policies, and gates.
Structures responses for feature design and refactoring tasks with clear implementation steps.
limitations: It is intended for Laravel projects, not general PHP or non-PHP backend work.
It does not assume cloud infrastructure or microservice architecture unless requested.
It prefers Laravel-native solutions and may not suggest third-party packages first.
It needs project context to produce precise file structure and migration guidance.

use_cases.title: Design a Laravel Feature
use_cases.description: Plan a new backend feature with routes, controllers, services, validation, authorization, resources, and tests.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Laravel Code
use_cases.description: Move business logic out of controllers, reduce duplication, and align code with Laravel conventions.

use_cases.title: Review API Quality
use_cases.description: Evaluate API responses, validation, authorization, pagination, rate limiting, and database access patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Simple Controller
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Laravel controller for validation, authorization, readability, and framework conventions. Explain the top issues first.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CRUD Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Laravel CRUD feature for this domain model. Include routing, validation, policies, resources, and service responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Service Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Laravel service flow to reduce coupling, improve testability, and preserve existing behavior. Explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an API Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Laravel API module for authorization gaps, validation risks, N+1 queries, transaction boundaries, and response consistency.

output_examples.input: Design a Laravel API endpoint for creating orders.
output: Architecture overview with routes, controller action, FormRequest validation, policy checks, service layer, resource response, and job boundaries.
Notes on transactions, idempotency, eager loading, and expected validation errors.

output_examples.input: Review a controller that validates input inside each action.
output: Findings that highlight repeated validation, missing authorization, and possible mass assignment risk.
A refactoring plan that moves validation to FormRequest classes and business logic to a service.

output_examples.input: Improve an endpoint with slow database queries.
output: Recommendations for eager loading, query scopes, pagination, indexes, and cache invalidation rules.
A short explanation of how each change affects correctness and performance.

best_practices: Provide the Laravel version, related models, routes, policies, and failing tests when asking for implementation help.
Ask for security, authorization, validation, and database behavior to be reviewed together.
Request tradeoffs when choosing between services, jobs, events, observers, and policies.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for non-Laravel PHP architecture decisions.
Do not ask for raw queries or mass assignment shortcuts without explaining the safety constraints.
Do not expect cloud, queue, cache, or package choices without project requirements.

faq.question: What Laravel versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets modern Laravel projects, especially Laravel 10 and Laravel 11 or later.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication and authorization?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Laravel-native auth, Sanctum for APIs, policies, gates, and secure password handling.

faq.question: Does it generate complete Laravel code?
faq.answer: It is designed to provide production-ready examples with namespaces, return types, and framework conventions.

faq.question: Can it review existing Laravel code?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies structural issues, security risks, performance problems, and Laravel-native improvements.

faq.question: Does it require third-party packages?
faq.answer: No. It prefers Laravel-native solutions and suggests packages only when the project context supports them.

faq.question: Can it design database performance improvements?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend eager loading, scopes, pagination, transactions, caching, and safer query patterns.
